author: product-requirements-expert
title: Filter the veterinarian directory by specialty
summary: Both veterinarian directory surfaces (the page and the machine-readable form) can be narrowed to a single specialty, showing only veterinarians who hold it. Whole-name, case-insensitive match; blank or absent value lists everyone; no match yields the normal directory with no vets listed.
acceptance_criteria: Given a specialty the clinic holds, when the directory page is narrowed to it, only veterinarians holding that specialty are listed, a page at a time
Given a specialty the clinic holds, when the machine-readable form is narrowed to it, only veterinarians holding that specialty are returned
Given a specialty name differing only by letter case, the directory matches it; given only part of a held specialty name, it does not match
Given a specialty no veterinarian holds, the directory is shown in its normal form with no veterinarians listed, neither an error nor a none-found message
Given no specialty, or one that is only spaces, every veterinarian is listed as when unfiltered
Given no specialty, both surfaces behave as before this requirement
notes: REQ-VET-003 reinstates the machine-readable directory as a supported surface (the endpoint code already exists; reinstatement is a PRD status change). This slice implements the specialty filter across both surfaces and exercises REQ-VET-003 via the JSON tests. Specialty match is whole-name case-insensitive, deliberately NOT the prefix match of owner search (REQ-OWN-002). Not reviewed here: the ADR index table in docs/adr/README.md needs the new non-goal ADR row added by system-design-expert (outside product-requirements-expert write scope).

author: system-design-expert
architectural_fit: Extends the existing vet-directory pattern (system-design § Contracts, VetController + cached VetRepository.findAll + Vets wrapper) with an optional specialty filter on both routes. No new type, module, or integration. The filter is applied in application code over the cached full collection (equalsIgnoreCase on Specialty name, whole-name), then paginated for the HTML route — filter-before-page. This is deliberately NOT a database-delegated match: it is vendor-invariant and does not reproduce the PostgreSQL case-sensitivity defect that owner last-name search carries (see system-design Known Defects). system-design § Contracts updated: VetController now implements REQ-VET-001/003/004, Vets implements REQ-VET-003, a directory-filtering note added, and the stale 'machine-readable route serves no requirement' Known Defect removed (REQ-VET-003 reinstates the route). docs/adr/README.md index gains the non-goal ADR row.
integration_points: VetController.showVetList gains @RequestParam(required=false) String specialty; blank/whitespace-only treated as absent (StringUtils.hasText). Absent -> today's exact path (findAll(pageable)). Present -> filter cached findAll() by specialty (case-insensitive whole-name over Vet.getSpecialties() names), then build a Page over the filtered list so pagination applies to the filtered set
VetController.showResourcesVetList (JSON, REQ-VET-003) applies the same specialty filter to findAll() before wrapping in Vets; absent/blank returns the full collection unchanged

vetList.html pagination links must carry the active specialty param (append &specialty=... to each th:href) so navigating pages preserves the filter; controller must expose the specialty value back to the model
A shared private helper in VetController (filter a Collection<Vet> by specialty) keeps HTML and JSON paths consistent

patterns.description: existing findPaginated/addPaginationModel helper the filtered HTML path extends (page the filtered list rather than delegating paging to findAll(pageable))
owner search uses findByLastNameStartingWith (prefix, DB-delegated). The specialty filter is the deliberate contrast: whole-name equality, case-folded in Java

risks.risk: Repeating owner search's PostgreSQL trap by delegating case-folding to the database (a derived findBySpecialties_NameIgnoreCase or JPQL relying on collation could pass H2 tests yet fail on PostgreSQL, invisibly per Known Defects)
risks.mitigation: Recommended design folds case in Java (equalsIgnoreCase), which is vendor-invariant and fully exercised by the H2 test suite

risks.risk: Caching the filter on a user-supplied specialty key would grow the unevicted 'vets' cache without bound (Open Question 5 notes no eviction)
risks.mitigation: Do not add a @Cacheable method keyed on the specialty; filter in-memory over the already-cached findAll() result

risks.risk: Pagination applied before filtering would page the full list then filter a page, breaking per-page counts
risks.mitigation: Filter the full cached collection first, then construct the Page over the filtered list

risks.risk: Dropping the specialty param on pagination navigation would reset the filter on page change
risks.mitigation: Template appends the active specialty to every pagination href; controller returns the specialty to the model

notes: Verdict minor: query parameter + thin in-memory filter step over the existing pattern; no ADR of its own beyond the non-goal ADR already written (2026-08-05-non-goal-vet-directory-filter.md) — the in-memory/vendor-invariant choice is a straightforward implementation call with no genuine trade-off, recorded as current state in system-design rather than as an ADR. Divergence from the prd-entry file_targets: VetRepository.java is listed there but is NOT required under the recommended in-memory design (the filter reads through the existing cached findAll()); left it out of primary_paths intentionally. If the implementer instead pursues a repository query, the binding constraints are: use the IgnoreCase keyword (never rely on column collation), do not make it @Cacheable on the specialty key, and watch for Hibernate in-memory pagination (HHH000104) on a paged query that joins the EAGER specialties collection. Autofix audit: no design-doc-autofix records present, nothing to audit.

author: security-reviewer
approved_aspects: Reflected XSS at the specialty->pagination-href boundary is mitigated: the template uses the Thymeleaf @{/vets.html(specialty=${specialty})} URL-expression builder, which URL-encodes query-parameter values and HTML-escapes the resulting href attribute; the value is never placed in an unescaped output sink
No injection path in the filter: specialty is matched by an in-memory case-insensitive String equalsIgnoreCase over Vet.getSpecialties() names, not a SQL/JPQL/regex query
Unbounded cache-key growth forbidden by the design-block was not introduced: the filter reads through the already-cached findAll() and no @Cacheable method is keyed on the user-supplied specialty
JSON surface (/vets) applies the identical filterBySpecialty helper and returns the same Vet data as the HTML page, exposing nothing extra
Full-collection in-memory load per filtered request is acceptable for this cached sample-app scale and consistent with recorded security baseline NG-1 (DoS out of scope)

findings.fix: Extract private static final int PAGE_SIZE = 5; at the top of the class and replace both local int pageSize = 5; declarations with PAGE_SIZE.

findings.description: filterBySpecialty passes specialty as-is to equalsIgnoreCase without trimming it first. StringUtils.hasText accepts " radiology " (whitespace around a real name) as non-blank, so the value reaches the match but fails to equal "radiology". Owner search (OwnerController) trims its input before comparing. The PRD specifies only that a blank or spaces-only value behaves as absent; it does not say whether leading/trailing whitespace surrounding a real name should be stripped. Clarify whether specialty must be trimmed before matching (consistent with owner search) or whether the caller-supplied literal value is canonical.

author: test-reviewer

findings.description: No test can distinguish filter-before-page from filter-after-page. The fixture has 3 total vets and a page size of 5, so the full directory fits on one page — paginate(page, filtered) and a hypothetical filter(findPaginated(page)) return identical results. The design-block explicitly requires filter-before-page: filtering the full cached collection first, then paging the filtered list. A bug that reverses the order would leave every new test green. A non-vacuous test needs a fixture with more than 5 total vets, at least two matching the filter specialty, and a page request that would overflow if the wrong collection were paged — so that a filter-after-page implementation returns a wrong page count or a wrong element that the assertion catches.

The test asserts model().attribute("specialty", is("radiology")), which verifies the specialty value is in the model, but no test checks that the rendered HTML pagination hrefs include specialty=radiology. The design-block requirement is explicit: pagination links must carry the active specialty param. If the Thymeleaf expressions in vetList.html omitted specialty=${specialty} from every th:href, every existing test would still pass. An assertion on the response body (e.g. content().string(containsString("specialty=radiology"))) or a second page navigation that verifies the specialty is preserved would close this gap.

All 7 new test method names omit the "the" prefix required by the BDD naming school (the{Subject}Should{Outcome} per docs/testing-principles.md § Test Naming, e.g. theOwnerSearchShouldMatchOnLastNamePrefix). The prd-entry test_names field specifies the same names without "the", creating a conflict between the naming convention and the gate-check values. Both the prd-entry test_names and the test method names need updating together. Raising to product-requirements-expert to revise test_names; feature-implementer then renames the test methods to match.

The acceptance criterion "Given no specialty, both surfaces behave as before this requirement" is count-verified only for the JSON surface (absentSpecialtyShouldReturnTheFullDirectory asserts jsonPath("$.vetList", hasSize(3))). The HTML surface test showVetListHtml asserts model existence and view name but not vet count. Adding model().attribute("listVets", hasSize(3)) to showVetListHtml closes the backward-compatibility gap for the HTML surface.
findings.fix: Add .andExpect(model().attribute("listVets", hasSize(3))) to the showVetListHtml test after the existing model().attributeExists("listVets") expectation.
